statements.C1: Uses `github.com/spf13/cobra` for CLI routing and `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` for YAML/frontmatter parsing.
statements.C2: Implements ADR 0004 (strict level derivation from container location) and `docs/design/gradus-design.md` §9.1–§9.5.
statements.NFR1: **Zero CGO & Cross-Platform Paths:** All schema parsing, `init`, and `explain` operations MUST compile with `CGO_ENABLED=0` and handle both POSIX (`/`) and Windows (`\`) filesystem paths cleanly.
statements.NFR2: **Canonical English:** All generated files, error messages, CLI help text, and specifications MUST be written in English.
statements.NFR3: **Exit Code Determinism (D-73):** Configuration, schema, and lookup errors MUST strictly return exit code `2`, never `0`.
statements.R1.AC1: The system SHALL provide `spec/v1/SPEC.md` documenting the `gradus/v1` schema for `gradus.yaml`, `level.yaml`, `overlay.yaml`, rule Markdown frontmatter, `gradus.lock`, resolved views, evidence records, lessons, and exceptions.
statements.R1.AC2: The system SHALL provide valid JSON Schema files under `spec/v1/schema/` for `gradus`, `level`, `overlay`, `rule-frontmatter`, `lock`, `resolved-view`, `evidence`, `lesson`, and `exception`.
statements.R2.AC1: WHEN `internal/schema` parses a valid `gradus.yaml` (`schema: gradus/v1`, non-empty ordered `levels` with unique IDs matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`), the system SHALL return the typed pyramid configuration with zero errors.
statements.R2.AC2: IF `gradus.yaml`, `level.yaml`, or `overlay.yaml` contains malformed YAML, an unsupported `schema` value, duplicate level IDs, or a level ID failing `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, THEN the system SHALL return a descriptive validation error that maps to CLI exit code `2`.
statements.R2.AC3: WHEN `gradus.yaml`, `level.yaml`, or `overlay.yaml` contains unknown YAML keys, the system SHALL record each unknown key as a diagnostic note without failing validation.
statements.R2.AC4: WHEN `internal/schema` parses `level.yaml` or `overlay.yaml`, the system SHALL validate required metadata (`schema`, `id`) and optional governance sections (`owners`, `approvers`, `charter`, `constraints`, `exceptions`, and overlay `strength`/`activation`).
statements.R3.AC1: WHEN `internal/schema` parses a valid rule Markdown file, the system SHALL extract frontmatter fields (`id` matching `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(-[A-Z0-9]+)+$`, `title`, `severity` in `MUST|SHOULD|MAY`, `enforcement` defaulting to `prompt`, `scope` defaulting to `["**/*"]`, `overrides`, `overridable`, `checker`, `guard`, `tags`, `version`, `status` defaulting to `active`) and Markdown body sections (statement paragraph, `Why`, `Rationalizations`, and `Examples` with `Compliant`/`Non-compliant`).
statements.R3.AC2: IF a rule file is missing YAML frontmatter, misses `id`/`title`/`severity`/statement, uses an invalid `id`/`severity`/`enforcement`, or declares `enforcement: check` without `checker` or `enforcement: hook` without `guard`, THEN the system SHALL reject the file with a validation error.
statements.R3.AC3: The system SHALL derive a rule's effective `level` exclusively from its containing level container rather than its `id` prefix or frontmatter.
statements.R3.AC4: WHEN a rule frontmatter contains unknown YAML keys, the system SHALL record each unknown key as a diagnostic note without failing validation.
statements.R4.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl init` runs in a directory without `gradus.yaml`, the system SHALL create `gradus.yaml` (`schema: gradus/v1`), `.gradus/levels/project/level.yaml`, an example rule in `.gradus/levels/project/rules/`, and append missing Gradus git-ignore patterns (`.gradus/cache/`, `.gradus/evidence/`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.agents/rules/gradus-user-*.md`) to `.gitignore` while preserving existing `.gitignore` lines.
statements.R4.AC2: IF `gradus.yaml` already exists and `--force` is not specified, THEN `gradusctl init` SHALL leave existing files untouched and exit with code `2`.
statements.R4.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl init --json` succeeds, the system SHALL write a valid JSON summary containing the created and updated file paths to stdout and exit with code `0`.
statements.R5.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl explain <id>` is run for a rule present in local configured levels, the system SHALL print the rule ID, title, derived level, source, severity, enforcement, scope, statement, rationale, rejected rationalizations, examples, and `overrides` target if set, and exit with code `0`.
statements.R5.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl explain <id> --json` is run for an existing rule, the system SHALL emit structured JSON containing the rule metadata, derived level, source provenance, body fields, and any diagnostic notes, and exit with code `0`.
statements.R5.AC3: IF `<id>` is not found in any configured local level OR the repository configuration is missing/invalid, THEN `gradusctl explain <id>` SHALL print a diagnostic error to stderr and exit with code `2`.

statements.C1: Builds on `internal/schema` from F1 (`core-schema-init`) and adds `github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4` for scope glob comparison/matching.
statements.C2: Implements ADR 0001 (CI override restriction) and ADR 0004 (container-derived level).
statements.NFR1: **Performance:** `gradusctl status --brief` MUST complete in under 100ms on local cached pyramids with zero network I/O.
statements.NFR2: **Deterministic Subprocess Git (D-69):** Git source fetching MUST invoke the system `git` binary via `os/exec` with no CGO or `go-git` dependencies.
statements.NFR3: **Exit Code Semantics (D-73):** `0` = clean pass, `1` = conflicts/violations, `2` = error (lock tamper, missing ref/unreachable `fail-closed` source, unknown override target, invalid schema).
statements.R1.AC1: WHEN a level or overlay specifies `source.path`, the system SHALL resolve its directory on disk while skipping `~/` home-directory levels when the `CI` environment variable is set.
statements.R1.AC2: WHEN a level or overlay specifies `source.git` and `source.ref`, the system SHALL fetch the specified ref into `.gradus/cache/` using the system `git` binary via `os/exec` and record the resolved commit SHA.
statements.R1.AC3: IF a remote `source.git` is unreachable and `offline.mode` is `cache` with an unexpired cached copy within `max_age`, THEN the system SHALL use the cached copy and emit a diagnostic note.
statements.R1.AC4: IF a remote `source.git` is unreachable and `offline.mode` is `fail-closed` OR the cache is missing/expired, THEN the system SHALL fail resolution and exit with code `2`.
statements.R2.AC1: The system SHALL compute a deterministic SHA-256 hash over a level or overlay directory by sorting normalized slash paths lexicographically and normalizing `\r\n` line endings to `\n`.
statements.R2.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl resolve --write` succeeds, the system SHALL write `gradus.lock` containing `schema: gradus/v1`, `definition_hash`, `entries` for all non-`user` levels and overlays, and `view_hash`.
statements.R2.AC3: IF an existing `gradus.lock` is present and a `locked: true` level or overlay on disk or in cache has a hash differing from its recorded lock entry, THEN the system SHALL reject resolution as a lock integrity error and exit with code `2`.
statements.R3.AC1: WHEN resolving the pyramid, the system SHALL order levels as declared in `gradus.yaml`, insert each active overlay immediately after the level matching its `strength`, drop `retired` rules, exclude `draft` rules by default, and mark rules covered by unexpired exceptions in `.gradus/exceptions/` as waived for their scopes.
statements.R3.AC2: IF a lower-level definition violates inherited `constraints` from an upper level's `level.yaml` (`require_levels`, `max_extra_levels`, `allowed_overlays`), THEN the system SHALL report the constraint violation as a blocking conflict.
statements.R3.AC3: IF a lower-level rule declares `overrides: <ID>` targeting an unknown rule ID OR a committed level targets a `user`-level rule (ADR 0001), THEN the system SHALL fail resolution with exit code `2`.
statements.R3.AC4: IF a rule duplicates an existing rule ID without `overrides`, OR weakens `severity`, widens `scope`, or weakens `enforcement` on a non-overridable rule, OR overrides a rule in a `locked: true` level not listed in `editable_rules`, THEN the system SHALL record a blocking conflict in the resolved view.
statements.R3.AC5: WHEN confirmed semantic conflicts exist in `.gradus/findings/`, the system SHALL include them as blocking entries in `conflicts`.
statements.R4.AC1: WHEN `gradusctl resolve` runs on a conflict-free pyramid, the system SHALL emit the resolved view (including `view_hash`, `lock_hash`, `levels`, `overlays`, `rules`, `conflicts`, `exceptions`, and `budget`) as text or `--json` and exit with code `0`.
statements.R4.AC2: WHEN `gradusctl resolve` detects one or more blocking conflicts, the system SHALL still emit the resolved view with `conflicts` populated and exit with code `1`.
statements.R4.AC3: WHEN `gradusctl status` or `gradusctl status --brief` runs in a Gradus repository, the system SHALL report lock state, conflict count, and pending lesson count in text or `--json` without making network calls.
